decisions.title: Which context members are required at the envelope

decisions.title: A pinned schema_ref must resolve, or name the bounded context that owes it

decisions.taken: Every schema_ref value anywhere in the committed corpus must either resolve through the released registry or have its base URN on an explicit deferred allowlist naming the bounded context that owns it. The allowlist lives in config/deferred-schema-owners.json, because it is governance data and OWNERS.yaml assigns UNASSIGNED to everything it names, which makes it the only concrete ownership statement this repository holds. It is bound to the corpus in both directions: an entry nothing references is stale and fails, and where a document pins an owner_context beside the schema_ref, the allowlist's owner must agree. The swept corpus is fixtures/, examples/ AND schemas/ — a const in a released schema is a stronger statement than a fixture value, because it makes the document a requirement rather than an example.

Also rejected: requiring every schema_ref to resolve today, which would either delete shipped fixtures or force FND-002 to write schemas owned by FND-009C, FND-015 and six domain packages.
decisions.measurement_correction: This entry first said 14, which was wrong when it was written: the sweep measured 15 over fixtures/ alone. It is 16 once the corpus also carries an instance of document-version:1, which typed-refs:1 required and no fixture had. The number is no longer prose — tests/test_schema_ref_resolution.py::test_the_register_states_the_number_the_sweep_actually_measures asserts this field against the allowlist, and test_the_allowlist_is_exactly_the_set_of_unowned_documents asserts the allowlist against the corpus, so a hand-typed count cannot drift again. It is 17 after FND-002 task 4: evidence-location-version:1 LEFT the allowlist because the released registry now resolves it, and coordinate-manifest:1 and decomposition-block:1 joined it because the evidence corpus pins two documents (document 16 lines 851 and 859-861; implementation-plans/13-hirag-service.md lines 361-362) that nobody releases.

decisions.title: bbox is carried as decimal strings (FORCED by the hash profile), bounded to [0,1] and ordered x0 y0 x1 y1 (both LOCAL CHOICES)
citations: 10-existing-service-extension-specifications.md:207 — '"bbox": [0.10, 0.22, 0.91, 0.31]'
implementation-plans/00-shared-foundation.md:241-243 — canonical hash section 4.3, the exact-decimal rule
canonical-hash-profile.v1 and the released hash profile it derives — binary_float_policy is 'reject'
stable-identity.v1#/$defs/decimal_string — 'Exact decimal carried as a string; never an unstable binary float'
decisions.taken: An ordered four-member array of released decimal strings, each additionally bounded to [0,1] by a pattern beside the composed $ref, in the order [x0, y0, x1, y1]. The three parts have DIFFERENT standing and are recorded separately because they do. (1) The decimal-string CARRIER is forced, and forced by the released contract rather than by the citation: canonical-hash-profile:1 declares binary_float_policy: reject, so a bbox held as JSON numbers could never have its content_hash computed, and this record carries a content_hash by construction. (2) The [0,1] BOUND is a local choice. (3) The CORNER ORDER is a local choice.
decisions.rejected: Carrying the four values as JSON numbers, exactly as document 10 line 207 prints them. Rejected on the measured ground in (1) above: binary_float_policy is reject, so such a record could not be hashed at all. run-manifest:1 already carries its tolerance as a decimal string for the same reason. || REJECTED FOR THE [0,1] BOUND: leaving the values unbounded, which is what the corpus actually licenses. Taken anyway because a selector whose bbox is expressed in one producer's centimetres and another's fractions cannot be compared or re-rendered, and a bound that is wrong is discovered on the first out-of-range instance whereas an absent one is discovered by a mis-rendered citation. decisions.title: 'column/cell range' collapses to one member and 'line/column range' splits into two, because the two idioms are not the same idiom
citations: 10-existing-service-extension-specifications.md:216 — the tabular kind: 'sheet/table, stable row ID or row index, column/cell range and value hash'
10-existing-service-extension-specifications.md:220 — the code kind: 'repository/bundle version, commit/content hash, path and line/column range'
10-existing-service-extension-specifications.md:222 — 'Fields are optional only when the asset format cannot express them.'
decisions.taken: The tabular kind carries ONE required member, cell_range. The code kind carries TWO, a required line_range and an optional column_range. The two 'X/Y range' phrases have the same SHAPE and different MEANINGS, and the treatment follows the meaning. In a spreadsheet a column range and a cell range are two spellings of ONE address space and the cell range subsumes the column range -- C:C is expressible as a cell range, so one member of A1-style notation carries both readings and a second member could only ever restate part of the first. In source code a line range and a column range are ORTHOGONAL AXES: lines 118-142 and columns 5-61 are independent facts and neither subsumes the other, so collapsing them would make a column range usable where a line range is required with no gate anywhere able to see it. column_range is the optional half because line is the primary axis in the citation's own word order and because line 222 licenses optionality where the format cannot express the member -- a whole-line span has no column range.
decisions.rejected: Treating the two phrases alike, in either direction. Collapsing 'line/column range' to one code_range would lose the orthogonality above. Splitting 'column/cell range' into column_range + cell_range on the tabular kind would release two members that address the same cells in two notations, which is the 'two encodings of one fact' hazard IMP-DEC-FND002-001 rejects for the tenant discriminator and which would give one region two canonical hashes. Recorded because the two phrases are visibly parallel and the opposite treatment looks like an oversight until the reason is written down -- which, until 2026-08-02, it was not.
decisions.residual_risk: cell_range is a string with no grammar. A producer emitting 'C4:C4' and one emitting 'Sheet1!C4' both validate and do not compare equal. The corpus states no notation, so pinning one would be invention; it is left open deliberately and is the same class of gap as the bbox unit in IMP-DEC-FND002-026.

open_defects.title: The engines render an interpolated VALUE differently in eleven message sites, and two of them differ in shape rather than quoting
open_defects.status: OPEN — needs no decision, only the work. EXTENSIONS.md section 4.5 itself is CLOSED (see resolved_defects EXT-4.5); this is a DIFFERENT defect in the same messages, recorded separately so the closure cannot be read as covering it.
open_defects.mechanism: Python interpolates the offending value with repr() and the TypeScript port renders it as JSON. Re-measured 2026-08-04 over src/research_contracts/canonical/: of 32 !r interpolations, 17 name a pointer, rule, schema_ref or annotation and render identically in both languages, and ELEVEN message sites interpolate an arbitrary JSON value and therefore diverge -- hash_profile.py:788, hash_profile.py:804-805, hash_view.py:109, jcs.py:84, jcs.py:116, jcs.py:174, registry.py:301, structural.py:663, structural.py:695, structural.py:703 and structural.py:734. Nine diverge by scalar spelling: 'a' versus "a", True versus true, None versus null. TWO DIVERGE IN SHAPE, which is the part a quote-style framing misses: hash_profile.py:788 and :804-805 interpolate manifest entries -- lists and dicts -- and their counterparts at packages/typescript/src/hashProfile.ts:885 and :909 render through stableKey(), which SORTS object keys by code point and emits no spaces, while Python's !r preserves insertion order and emits ', '. The same manifest entry prints as {'pointer': '/x', 'kind': 'ordered'} in one engine and {"kind":"ordered","pointer":"/x"} in the other. EXTENSIONS.md section 9 item 12 states the rule this breaks: two engines that refuse the same input with different words are a divergence a consumer reading either one cannot reconcile.
open_defects.why_it_is_now_urgent: Not newly urgent, but newly VISIBLE and newly load-bearing. Section 4.5 shipped CLOSED on 2026-08-04 with a record that cannot detect this, and packages/typescript/src/structural.ts previously asserted the opposite in prose -- 'every message produced for a rule that a committed fixture actually exercises is byte-identical to Python's' -- which was measurably false. That sentence has been corrected rather than deleted. A closure whose own file claims byte-identity while the operator's most common message diverges is the shape that gets inherited as settled.
open_defects.what_it_breaks: Nothing on today's corpus, and that is a property of the CORPUS rather than of the engines, which is precisely why it is recorded rather than left to be rediscovered. NO GATE IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN SEE IT, and the strongest evidence is the one gate built to find cross-language divergence: src/research_contracts/tooling/differential_fuzz.py records a refusal as {"error": type(exc).__name__} at line 761 and compares expected["error"] != actual["error"] at line 876 — the error CLASS NAME only, never the message text. Its own module docstring says the run is green when both engines fail 'with the same error class name'. So the P8 fuzzer is blind to this entire class BY CONSTRUCTION, and would stay green over any number of randomly generated cases that hit all eleven sites. The rest of the corpus is silent for narrower reasons: the divergence is reachable on run-manifest:1, the one released disjoint rule that can fire, whose members are UUID strings; the committed fixture that exercises it (fixtures/foundation/v1/invalid/run-manifest-output-is-also-its-own-input.json) asserts only the rule name and 'must be disjoint'; and the new operator vectors deliberately use the number 7, which both languages render as 7. Both of those facts are disclosed in the vector record's own header rather than left for a reader to find. So nothing would notice this divergence, and nothing would notice it widening.
open_defects.options: A. Route every interpolated value in both engines through the shared rendering module (canonical/rendering.py json_text in Python, rendering.ts jsonText in the port), which already exists and which both engines already use for authoring-time refusal text. This is the whole fix and it introduces no new normative semantics. It also subsumes stableKey(), whose key-sorting is a second, independent divergence from Python that json_text does not have. B. Port repr() to TypeScript. Rejected on sight: repr is Python source syntax and the released contract is JSON. C. Leave it and document it, which is the current state and is what this entry exists to stop becoming permanent. A fourth option is NOT available: fixing the messages without also widening differential_fuzz.py to compare message text would close the defect while leaving the gate that missed it still unable to catch the next one.
open_defects.why_not_taken_here: It spans EXTENSIONS.md sections 4.1, 4.4 AND 4.5 at once -- the interval, uniqueness and disjointness diagnostics -- plus hash_profile's manifest-contradiction messages, and the branch that closed section 4.5 owned sections 4.2 and 4.5 only. Taking it would have required editing section 4.4's standing note ('the failure text still renders the value with Python repr; only the comparison is canonical bytes'), which belongs to another owner. Option A is small, and it is deferred for ownership reasons rather than difficulty.
open_defects.blocked_on: An owner for EXTENSIONS.md section 4.4, or a single agent given sections 4.1, 4.4 and 4.5 together plus hash_profile's two manifest messages. ELEVEN message sites per engine, not the three an earlier draft of this entry estimated: the count is listed in `mechanism` and was measured, not guessed. Widening differential_fuzz.py to compare message text belongs in the same change, or the fix ships with its own detector still blind.
open_defects.not_blocking: Section 4.5's closure, which is independent: the messages that closure ADDED interpolate pointers only and are byte-identical by construction, which is why the vector record can compare them byte for byte at all.

resolved_defects.title: An opaque subtree containing an array is unhashable
resolved_defects.status: CLOSED 2026-07-31 — REFUTED. The defect as recorded does not exist; no decision and no owner were ever needed.
resolved_defects.as_recorded: 'An opaque subtree containing an array is unhashable: declaring one flips _has_declared_children and then EVERY member of the subtree must be declared.' Recorded in the wave-2 register as a capability gap needing a spec-level rule-vocabulary decision (decision F).
resolved_defects.taken: The second clause is false and the entry is withdrawn. _ViewBuilder._declared_prefixes is derived from included_pointers | excluded_pointers alone and never from arrays, and merge_profile_extensions permits a domain to add arrays WITHOUT included_pointers (EXTENSIBLE_PROFILE_KEYS = {included_pointers, arrays}). An arrays-only profile extension therefore supplies the collection kind without adding a declared child: the subtree stays opaque and its undeclared members still pass. The envelope's two documented rules — 'declare one member, declare them all' and 'an array inside an opaque subtree still needs its own declaration' — are independent, and satisfying the second does not trigger the first.
resolved_defects.rejected: Treating it as a capability gap and escalating it to an owner — which is what the wave-2 register did. The capability already existed; what was missing was a test. Also rejected: deleting the entry outright, which would make a refuted defect indistinguishable from a forgotten one.
resolved_defects.what_remains_true_and_is_narrower: Two things. FIRST, the SCHEMA-ANNOTATION route is still blocked, and EXTENSIONS.md section 6.3 states it correctly at that narrower scope: to attach an x-datacompany-array at /value/tags a domain schema must reach it through a properties chain, and hash_profile._Walker adds every properties name to included_pointers, which does make /value a declared prefix. rc#16 proved the profile-extension route works; it did not test the annotation route, and this entry does not claim it was fixed. SECOND, the route rc#16 used is the escape hatch EXTENSIONS.md had already flagged as needing an explicit decision — it is now load-bearing rather than latent, and is carried forward as open defect D9 instead of being closed along with D4.
resolved_defects.root_cause: A test-coverage asymmetry read as a capability gap. Three assertions across two languages proved an array under an opaque subtree NEEDS a declaration; none proved one could be SUPPLIED. The absent green half read as an impossibility. This is the same failure mode as decision F's premise about D3: inferring a missing capability from a missing test.
resolved_defects.evidence: research_contracts#16. tests/test_canonical_hash.py::test_an_arrays_only_extension_declares_a_collection_inside_an_opaque_subtree and the matching TypeScript assertion in packages/typescript/test/hashView.test.ts, including the case where the opaque payload IS the array (bitemporal-assertion:1 /value is typed object|array|...). Both proven falsifiable: patching _declared_prefixes / declaredPrefixes to also consume arrays — making the code behave the way D4 claimed it already did — turns the Python test red with exactly D4's predicted UndeclaredPathError: /value/steps. No engine source changed and no hash is affected.
resolved_defects.avoided_anyway: run-manifest:1 declares its parameters as a typed collection rather than an opaque payload, so no released foundation schema depended on D4 either way. FND-002 task 4 follows the same precedent: locator selectors are declared named members, not an x-datacompany-hash-opaque bag.
resolved_defects.precision_note_2026-08-02: D4 is NOT reopened and its conclusion is unchanged; two sentences above became imprecise when a SEPARATE defect was fixed in hash_view. The defect: _declared_prefixes is derived from included_pointers | excluded_pointers, so an exclusion strictly BELOW an opaque pointer — 'exclude the signature from an opaque payload', the motivating case for the two annotations existing at all — injected the payload into the prefix set and revoked the subtree's opacity, and every undeclared SIBLING of the signature then raised UndeclaredPathError. The opacity decision now consults a NARROWER set, _ViewBuilder._included_prefixes / ViewBuilder.includedPrefixes, derived from included_pointers alone, because opacity is revoked by a DECLARED MEMBER — which is what the released $comment on bitemporal-assertion:1 /value says — and an exclusion is the opposite act. Consequences for this record, both of them tested: (1) 'taken' stays literally true — _declared_prefixes is still derived from included_pointers | excluded_pointers alone and never from arrays — and the closure argument survives a fortiori, since arrays contribute to neither set, but the set that now DECIDES opacity is _included_prefixes; (2) 'evidence' names a falsification recipe that no longer falsifies: patching _declared_prefixes / declaredPrefixes alone to consume arrays now leaves the test GREEN. The recipe that reproduces D4's predicted 'UndeclaredPathError: /value/steps' is patching BOTH prefix sets, or _included_prefixes alone (which raises one level higher, at /value, as neither-declared-nor-opaque). What survives is what mattered: an arrays-only profile extension still adds no declared child and the subtree still stays opaque. See tests/test_hash_view_opaque_exclusion.py and packages/typescript/test/engineDefects.test.ts.
resolved_defects.still_true_after_the_precision_note: The schema-annotation route recorded under what_remains_true_and_is_narrower is UNAFFECTED and is still blocked: hash_profile._Walker puts every properties name into included_pointers, and an included pointer is exactly what still revokes opacity. tests/test_foundation_schemas.py::test_d4_the_schema_annotation_route_into_an_opaque_subtree_is_still_blocked and D9's mechanism sentence both continue to hold.

resolved_defects.title: A cross-field rule was unevaluable at every child-keyword position, which blocked FND-002 task 4
resolved_defects.status: CLOSED 2026-07-30 as option B — an additive `scope` member on a cross-field rule. Decided by George against docs/D3-DECISION-BRIEF.md.
resolved_defects.scope_of_the_defect: 48 of 48 cells: EIGHT released rule-bearing schemas x six child positions, all raising. The brief and the wave-2 register both said 30 of 30 across five schemas; that undercount omitted page:1#/$defs/page_request, research-access-context:1 and run-manifest:1. Corrected here and in EXTENSIONS.md section 6.1.
resolved_defects.taken: Rules gain an optional `scope`: `absolute` (the default, and the meaning of every rule released before D3) resolves operands against the instance root; `relative` resolves them against the location the rule was reached at, and is evaluated once per addressed instance location. All 13 released rules were annotated `relative`, which is meaning-preserving because the two bases coincide at a document root — asserted by tests/test_d3_relative_scope.py::test_relative_and_absolute_agree_exactly_at_a_document_root, not assumed.
resolved_defects.rejected: Option A (relative by default) — correct, and the cheapest moment for it since the TypeScript cross-field evaluator did not yet exist, but it re-reads every released operand and is a vocabulary version 2. Option C (re-declare the rule at each composing root) — proven to evaluate, report NOTHING and assert a different proposition while looking identical, and forbidden by pinned-version-ref's own $comment. Option D (embed only rule-free shapes) — solves an engine problem by editing the domain model.
resolved_defects.cost_accepted: A FOURTH lexically identical pointer language (EXTENSIONS.md section 1.4). Nothing in an operand's text distinguishes the two readings; `scope` is the only discriminator and must be read before any operand is interpreted.
resolved_defects.kept_deliberately: An absolute-scoped rule below a child keyword still raises, and `contains`/`propertyNames` raise at ANY scope. Failing closed was the one good property of the pre-D3 behaviour and option B does not weaken it.
resolved_defects.evidence: tests/test_d3_relative_scope.py — 160 checks: the 48 cells now evaluate AT the child location, with a per-position false-positive control requiring silence where the subschema applies nowhere, a regression guard that an un-opted-in rule still raises, and the root-equivalence proof. resolved_defects.mechanism: canonical-hash-profile.v1#/$defs/hash_view_pointer requires a leading '/' and minLength 2, so neither '/' nor RFC 6901's whole-document '' is a legal order_key entry; and hash_view._pointer_at resolves an order key only inside a dict member, so a scalar member always yields the absent marker and raises MissingOrderKeyError. resolved_defects.taken: A new canonical-hash-profile definition, order_key_pointer, admitting RFC 6901's whole-document pointer "" in addition to hash_view_pointer; hash_view._pointer_at (and the TypeScript pointerAt) resolve it to the array MEMBER ITSELF. resolved_defects.title: A runtime profile extension can declare an array that no schema annotation can express
resolved_defects.status: CLOSED 2026-08-03 — FIXED. A new registered annotation, x-datacompany-hash-declaration-only (vocabulary 1.1 -> 1.2), makes the schema route derive a manifest BYTE-IDENTICAL to the runtime-merged one, so the escape hatch rc#16 refuted D4 through is no longer the only route. EXTENSIONS.md section 6.3.1 is rewritten from OPEN to closed; section 3.6 is the annotation's declaration. open_defects is now EMPTY.
resolved_defects.as_recorded: merge_profile_extensions accepts caller-supplied extensions directly, and validate_profile_against_schema only checks that the RELEASED entries are present unchanged — it permits extras. So merge_profile_extensions(profile, {"arrays": [{"pointer": "/value/tags", "kind": "ordered"}]}) succeeds on a subtree whose array cannot be annotated in any committed schema, because hash_profile._Walker would put the annotated pointer into included_pointers and destroy the opacity (see D4).
resolved_defects.taken: The register's option (a), in its NARROW form: an annotation whose pointer does not enter included_pointers, so both routes agree from the schema side. x-datacompany-hash-declaration-only: true says 'this schema node is reached only to carry annotations; it does not declare a hashed path'. The node is still walked and its x-datacompany-array still reaches the manifest's `arrays`; what is removed is the node's own pointer, and every pointer beneath it, from included_pointers — so the enclosing x-datacompany-hash-opaque subtree keeps its opacity. Four implementation constraints, each with a test that would catch its absence: (1) COLLECT THEN POST-FILTER, never suppress inline at the properties loop — the flag can arrive through a $ref or an allOf/anyOf/oneOf/then/else branch AFTER that loop has already added the pointer, so an inline check is composition-order dependent and two implementations composing differently diverge in silence; (2) FILTER BY PREFIX, matching the released exclusion cascade — an array OF OBJECTS also yields /value/tags/-/id from the items walk, and an exact-match filter would leave those in included_pointers, making /value a declared prefix again and revoking exactly the opacity the annotation preserves; (3) `arrays` is NEVER filtered by it, which is the whole point, and §5.2's released arrays exact-match quirk must NOT be generalised to this cascade; (4) the flag is legal only STRICTLY under an x-datacompany-hash-opaque pointer and derivation RAISES otherwise. Ported to TypeScript in the same change, with byte-identical message text, because EXTENSIONS.md section 9 item 12 itself states that a one-language annotation here is a cross-language split.
resolved_defects.rejected: Option (c) — 'ratify runtime-only array declarations and tighten validate_profile_against_schema to accept ONLY the extras EXTENSIBLE_PROFILE_KEYS names' — which this register recorded as 'the smallest, and what #16 implicitly assumed'. REJECTED BECAUSE IT IS ALREADY ENFORCED AND WOULD HAVE CHANGED NOTHING. See the correction below. Also rejected: option (a) in its BLANKET form — suppressing every pointer under an opaque subtree — which erases /value/other along with /value/tags and so destroys a released capability: declaring ALL members of an opaque subtree, thereby revoking its opacity, works today and is mandated by bitemporal-assertion:1 /value itself ('the moment a domain declares any member of value, it must declare all of them'). Also rejected: option (b), 'a derivation rule that opacity survives array-only declarations' — 'array-only' is not a property the walker can observe; it would have to INFER that a properties name exists solely to reach an annotation, which is precisely the fact the author now states outright. Also rejected: converting run-manifest:1 /inputs/parameters to an opaque bag now that it is expressible — that changes which paths reach included_pointers and is canonical-hash-affecting, so it is a separate decision with its own evidence, not a consequence of this annotation existing. Only its stale $comment was updated.
resolved_defects.correction_option_c_was_a_no_op: MEASURED, and it corrects this register's own options text. (c) claimed there was looseness in validate_profile_against_schema to tighten. There is none, in either half: an unknown TOP-LEVEL manifest key is already rejected by canonical-hash-profile.v1's additionalProperties:false through validate_hash_profile — reproduced: "HashProfileError: hash-view manifest is not a valid urn:datacompany:canonical-hash-profile:1: <root>: Additional properties are not allowed ('bogus_key' was unexpected)" — and a non-extensible EXTENSION key is already rejected inside merge_profile_extensions — reproduced: "HashProfileError: a domain extension may only add included_pointers and arrays, not ['excluded_pointers']". The 'smallest available change' was therefore a no-op that would have left the two routes still disagreeing, which is why the durable route was taken. Recorded here and in EXTENSIONS.md section 6.3.1 so the superseded options text cannot be read back as an untried alternative.
resolved_defects.correction_the_blanket_form_was_disquali: Also measured rather than judged. 'Suppress everything under an opaque subtree' reads like the same fix and is not: it revokes a capability the released corpus mandates. tests/test_hash_view_opaque_exclusion.py::test_a_declared_member_of_an_opaque_subtree_still_revokes_opacity is that capability's false-positive control and stays green against the narrow form, because the narrow form suppresses only what an author explicitly flags.
resolved_defects.hash_impact: NONE on the committed corpus, measured with a positive control rather than argued. All 18 released schemas were re-derived before and after the change and the manifests are byte-identical (empty diff). A zero measurement is not evidence without a control, so the same harness was run twice more against deliberately perturbed corpora and reported a non-empty diff each time: (i) planting x-datacompany-hash-declaration-only plus an x-datacompany-array on bitemporal-assertion:1 /value adds {"kind":"ordered","pointer":"/value/tags"} to `arrays` and — correctly — nothing to included_pointers; (ii) deleting the released x-datacompany-hash-excluded on stable-identity:1 /aggregate_version moves excluded_pointers and included_pointers in two schemas. The first control is the on-point one: it proves the harness would have SEEN the new rule if any committed schema used it, not merely that `diff` works. DERIVATION_PROFILE_VERSION therefore did not bump for this change, by EXTENSIONS.md section 1.3's own rule, which makes adding a NAME a minor vocabulary bump and reserves a profile_version bump for changing what an EXISTING annotation means. No previously computed content_hash is invalidated. Vocabulary 1.1 -> 1.2 follows the D3 precedent recorded in the meta-schema's $comment: the $id and filename stay at v1 because every rule released before the addition keeps its meaning. CORRECTED FRAMING 2026-08-04: this empty diff proves the change is INERT ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS -- the blast-radius question -- and NOT that it is correct. Disabling the annotation entirely produces the identical zero, for the identical reason: no released schema uses it. Correctness rests on the two-route byte equality and the fixture corpus. The same caveat applies to any integration proof that quotes an empty manifest delta as evidence the change is sound.
resolved_defects.decisions_beyond_the_corpus: LABELLED, because this register's previous entry correctly noted that nothing in document 16 or the shared-foundation plan speaks to D9, so recording an answer as 'derived' would be inventing normative semantics. Two rules are DECISIONS TAKEN BY THE REPOSITORY OWNER, who asked for the durable fix over the smallest, and neither is derivable from the corpus: (1) the flag is legal ONLY strictly inside an x-datacompany-hash-opaque subtree — outside one it would silently remove a member from the hash view with no reason and no excluded_pointers entry, a second and reasonless spelling of x-datacompany-hash-excluded; and strictly UNDER rather than AT, because allowing both annotations on one node would satisfy the guard trivially and let any author suppress any pointer anywhere. (2) An opaque subtree may not BOTH declare a member and carry the flag — the released 'declare none or declare all' rule; a declared sibling revokes the opacity and the declaration-only pointer is then the one member that cannot be declared, so the shape raises UndeclaredPathError at HASH time, far from the schema that caused it. Grouped by each flag's NEAREST opaque ancestor, so nested opaque subtrees are not refused. Both turn a confusing runtime failure into a named derivation refusal; both are recorded as decisions, not derivations.
resolved_defects.a_rule_that_was_written_and_deleted: Recorded because the deletion is the honest part. The meta-schema originally also required x-datacompany-array or x-datacompany-cross-field BESIDE the flag, reasoning that a node 'reached only to carry annotations' that carries none declares nothing. That rule REJECTED A LEGAL SHAPE: because the suppression cascades by prefix, the intended way to declare a DEEP array is one flag on the OUTERMOST node of the properties chain, and that node carries only `properties`. The false-positive control caught it before it shipped. What remains is the limit, recorded in EXTENSIONS.md section 8.1 rather than replaced by a rule that reads strict and is wrong: a declaration-only node that reaches no annotation is NOT detected. It is inert — its member still hashes through the enclosing opacity — and the shapes that are not inert are the three the engine refuses. tests/test_extension_vocabulary.py::test_a_declaration_only_node_that_carries_only_properties_is_accepted keeps the deleted rule from being re-added silently.
resolved_defects.evidence: THE CLOSURE IS AN EQUALITY, NOT A CAPABILITY: 'both routes work' would be satisfied by two routes that disagree. tests/test_declaration_only_annotation.py::test_the_two_routes_agree_byte_for_byte_on_the_released_opaque_subtree asserts that the manifest derived from an annotated mirror of the RELEASED bitemporal-assertion:1 — the exact shape the defect was written about — is byte-identical under RFC 8785 to merge_profile_extensions(derive_hash_profile(ref), {arrays:[{pointer:'/value/tags',kind:'ordered'}]}), with a non-vacuity check that both actually carry the declaration. The same assertion exists in packages/typescript/test/declarationOnly.test.ts. Committed as data in fixtures/canonical-hash/v1/declaration-only/ — five self-contained fixtures (two `derives`, three `rejects`), each carrying its own probe schema, the expected manifest as RFC 8785 canonical BYTES, and for the `derives` pair the runtime-route extension whose merged manifest must be byte-identical. Replayed by both engines with a count pinned as an EQUALITY that each reads from the other. Every new test was mutation-proven: removing the post-filter, making it exact-match instead of prefix, filtering `arrays` too, dropping the outside-opaque guard, dropping the declare-some guard, and moving the suppression inline into the properties loop were each planted, the naming test confirmed RED, and the break reverted. The mutations and their red output are in the commit body.
resolved_defects.root_cause: A released contract stated in TWO schema $comments a capability the derivation could not express, and nothing executed the contradiction. bitemporal-assertion.v1 /value said 'Arrays inside it still require their own ordered/set-like declaration'; canonical-hash-profile.v1 `arrays` said an undeclared array is rejected 'including inside an opaque subtree'. Jointly they demanded a declaration no committed schema could write. The gap was visible only in prose — run-manifest.v1 /inputs/parameters even documented the workaround it took to DODGE it — until rc#16 made the runtime escape hatch load-bearing by refuting D4 through it. That is the pattern this register keeps finding: a defect that lives in $comments and blockquotes, where no gate can reach it.
resolved_defects.knock_on: run-manifest.v1 /inputs/parameters refused x-datacompany-hash-opaque BECAUSE of D9, and its $comment asserted that 'No schema annotation can supply that declaration inside an opaque subtree'. That is now released prose asserting an impossibility that no longer holds, so it was rewritten to state what is true, with the correction dated. The schema's SHAPE is deliberately unchanged (see `rejected`). Pinned by tests/test_declaration_only_annotation.py::test_the_run_manifest_comment_no_longer_claims_the_route_is_impossible, which asserts both halves: the stale sentence is gone AND the parameters array is still a declared set-like collection with no x-datacompany-hash-opaque.
resolved_defects.open_defects_is_now_empty: D9 was the last entry. An empty open_defects is a state this register has not been in before and it must not be read as 'nothing is left': when D9 closed, EXTENSIONS.md section 6.4 recorded a decision that had NOT been taken (x-datacompany-composition-point was read by no code in either language, and had to be given an implementation or retired), and section 0.1 recorded that vocabulary ownership is unresolved. Neither was a defect, so neither belonged here. Section 6.4 has SINCE been taken and is recorded in this register as EXT-6.4 -- implemented rather than retired, so the annotation now has two readers -- which leaves section 0.1's ownership question as the only one of the two still live. The warning itself is unaffected and is why this note survives the correction: an empty open_defects has never meant an empty docket.
resolved_defects.refutation_2026_08_03: An independent refuter attacked the branch and found NO fail-open: the annotation cannot weaken a hash view, cannot revoke an exclusion, and cannot make two distinct instances hash identically. It reproduced the zero manifest delta with three further positive controls, confirmed the byte-identity closure independently, reproduced every mutation as RED, and could not break the post-filter through allOf/anyOf/oneOf/then/else, a $ref, a $ref cycle, a declaration split across branches, /value/tag versus /value/tags, or a ~1-escaped sibling. THREE BLOCKING DEFECTS AND FIVE CORRECTIONS were nevertheless real, and every one was the same shape -- the fix not reaching as far as this record claimed. (1) HIGH: the declare-none-or-declare-all rule read the RAW walk, where an excluded member is still a properties name, so it counted an EXCLUSION as a declaration that revokes opacity and REFUSED the signed opaque payload -- /value opaque, /value/sig excluded, /value/tags flagged -- which is the shape x-datacompany-hash-opaque and x-datacompany-hash-excluded exist for TOGETHER, and the one case D9 is really about. The runtime escape hatch hashed it correctly throughout, so D9 was NOT closed for the motivating case. hash_view states the governing rule in as many words: 'Opacity is revoked by a DECLARED MEMBER and by nothing else. An EXCLUSION is the opposite act.' Fixed by running the rule against the DERIVED included_pointers. (2) The 'byte-identical message text' parity was true only for ASCII: json.dumps defaults to ensure_ascii=True and JSON.stringify does not escape, and every fixture was ASCII, so the assertion was vacuous in the only dimension where it can fail. (3) The committed-fixture half of the closure evidence was vacuous: both engines read equivalent_runtime_route through optional access, so deleting it from every derives fixture left both suites at UNCHANGED passing counts. Corrections: the 'strictly under, never AT' rule was walk-past-able one level deeper by putting both annotations on a node inside another opaque subtree; the comment justifying an unfiltered opaque_pointers was false; the headline BYTE equality was an accident of sort order, because derive sorts arrays and merge_profile_extensions appended; and the D4-residue test was left un-rewritten beside an empty open_defects. All fixed, each with a committed fixture and a mutation.
resolved_defects.what_was_unpinned_in_both_directions: Recorded because it is the lesson, not the incident. TWO of the three blocking defects admitted two DIFFERENT fixes that each left all 1251 tests green -- the excluded-member rule (apply the exclusion cascade before the guard, or skip excluded pointers inside it) and the arrays sort order. A defect no test distinguishes is a defect the next session re-introduces by choosing the other fix, so each now has a committed fixture pinning the BEHAVIOUR and a mutation proving the fixture fires. The same applies to the vacuous fixture evidence: a conditional assertion (`if runtime is not None`) is not a pin, and what makes it one is a floor on how many fixtures must carry the member at all.
resolved_defects.citation_rot_found_while_fixing_it: COUNTS CORRECTED 2026-08-04 after a second refutation; the first telling of this inflated them. Measured against 46062b1: FOURTEEN distinct <module>.py:<line> citations shipped -- 10 in EXTENSIONS.md, 3 in the released meta-schema $comment, 1 in a released TypeScript source. (The earlier claim of FIFTEEN counted the second endpoint of a range citation such as hash_view.py:162,170 as a separate reference.) Their first line landed on a BLANK line once, on an unrelated `#:` comment four times, and on real code nine times -- where 'real code' still included :105 pointing at a bare `self,` parameter and :92 pointing at `self.excluded = {}` while claiming to show `is True`. THIRTEEN were converted to symbol citations; the fourteenth, in packages/typescript/src/hashProfile.ts, survived because the sweep read only two documents. TWO distinct pre-existing symbol citations were also wrong (hash_view._build_object and hash_view._is_declared_opaque, naming _ViewBuilder methods as module-level functions; three occurrences once this session's own new prose had added another). The earlier claim of '18 corrected' was occurrence-counting on top of the inflated line count; the measured figure is 13 line citations plus 2 distinct symbol citations.
resolved_defects.the_gate_that_closed_the_class_could_not: The sharpest finding of the second refutation, and the reason the first fix did not hold. Both citation patterns REQUIRED BACKTICKS. The released meta-schema writes its citations as bare text inside JSON $comment strings, so the sweep matched 0 of its 13 citations and 29 of EXTENSIONS.md's -- while a single shared `checked >= 12` floor, satisfied entirely by EXTENSIONS.md, made it read as measured. The class-killer test therefore could not fire on the one document whose three broken citations started the census: planting an unbackticked `hash_profile.py:9999` into the released meta-schema left the suite at 91 passed, exit 0. In the SAME commit that added the gate, renaming _require_declaration_only_inside_an_opaque_subtree left that dead name cited in two released artifacts -- the meta-schema's own hash_declaration_only declaration and hashProfile.ts -- and 1264 tests stayed green. FIXED: backticks are optional, every document carries its OWN floor (CITATION_FLOORS), the released TypeScript sources are scanned (comment text only, since `errors.length` and `registry.get` are ordinary code that the symbol pattern would otherwise report as fabricated findings), and the sweep asserts it found TypeScript sources at all rather than globbing to [] in silence. Fixing the gate immediately exposed three of its own defects: file extensions read as symbols (`structural.ts`), module-level AnnAssign constants missing from the AST symbol table so `hash_profile.DERIVATION_PROFILE_VERSION` reported as resolving to nothing, and TypeScript-to-TypeScript references (`jcs.esNumberToString`) mis-attributed to Python -- each a FALSE finding, which is the failure mode that gets a gate weakened rather than repaired. ACKNOWLEDGED LIMIT, recorded in the test's own docstring rather than left to read as stronger: the symbol check is EXISTENCE-ONLY, so a citation moved to a real-but-wrong sibling symbol stays green.
resolved_defects.cross_language_sort_order_was_unpinned: The C3 fix made merge_profile_extensions sort `arrays`; nothing asserted WHICH order. Python's `sorted` compares code POINTS and JavaScript's `<` and bare `.sort()` compare UTF-16 code UNITS, and they disagree for astral characters -- the same G1 divergence class this repository already carries an order-key fixture for, and the same shape as the ensure_ascii defect fixed one commit earlier. Both engines were in fact correct, but rewriting compareCodePoints with split('') or sortedStrings with a bare .sort() left all 701 TypeScript tests and all 37 Python declaration-only tests green. Now pinned in both suites with U+FF21 (one UTF-16 unit, 65313) against U+1F600 (a surrogate pair starting 0xD83D, 55357): code-point order puts U+FF21 first, UTF-16 order puts U+1F600 first, and the merged manifest's canonical bytes are asserted as the SAME literal on both sides so neither engine can agree with its own recomputation. Both mutations now go red.
resolved_defects.why_this_register_is_not_itself_swept: MEASURED AND DECIDED, not overlooked. config/foundation-decisions.json is a released config artifact of the meta-schema's shape and carries 11 symbol references and 2 `<module>.py:<line>` strings. Every one is NARRATION ABOUT citations rather than a citation: the two line strings quote the historical defect ('hash_view.py:162,170 counted as a separate reference', 'planting an unbackticked hash_profile.py:9999'), and the five that do not resolve are this register quoting the WRONG spellings it corrected (hash_view._build_object, hash_view._is_declared_opaque) or the false-positive examples the gate had to learn to ignore (errors.length, registry.get, jcs.esNumberToString). Zero live defects. Adding the file to the sweep would therefore forbid this register from QUOTING the defects it exists to record -- a gate that fights its own evidence -- and the only honest ways out are a quoting convention or an exemption marker, both of which are vocabulary decisions rather than repairs. Recorded as a deliberate exclusion with the measurement, so the next session neither re-litigates it nor adds the file naively and mangles accurate history.
resolved_defects.the_typescript_half_of_the_sweep_was_pin: Round 3. The round-2 repair added packages/typescript/src/*.ts to the citation sweep, and that claim was true for 3 of the 20 candidate references and pinned for 1 of the 11 files. Three defects, all in the NEW claim rather than in the two documents the gate was built for. (1) TS_SYMBOL_CITATION was narrowed to the modules hash_profile|hash_view on an ambiguity argument -- that jcs/structural/registry/errors are spelled the same in both languages -- and the corpus falsified that argument: the discriminator is the TAIL, not the module, because a Python name carries an UNDERSCORE where the TypeScript name is camelCase (jcs.es_number_to_string against jcs.esNumberToString). Eight real citations were unread, every one of which resolves in Python today: structural._OPERANDS, structural._LEGACY_SCHEMA_KEYWORDS, structural._UNLOCATABLE_KEYWORDS, structural._DEFINITION_BAG_KEYWORDS, structural._UNCOLLECTED_SCHEMA_KEYWORDS, registry.ecma_262_pattern, registry.schema_failure_codes, jcs.es_number_to_string. The tail rule scans 11 and correctly ignores the 9 that are ordinary code (errors.length, errors.join) or TypeScript siblings. (2) _comment_text kept only lines whose STRIPPED form began with //, * or /*, so every TRAILING comment was dropped -- `const x = 1;  // see hash_profile.py:9999` was invisible, which is exactly the class the line-number gate exists to kill, in a file the sweep had just been extended to cover. Its stated justification was also FALSE: it claimed whole-file scanning would read errors.length and registry.get as citations, and neither matched the pattern it was protecting. Filter deleted; the whole file is read. (3) Only hashProfile.ts carried a floor, so glob('hashProfile.ts') and glob('h*.ts') both left the suite green. Per-file floors now cover structural.ts, json.ts and registry.ts, and the number of .ts sources swept is an EQUALITY (11) rather than a floor, because a file APPEARING is as much a change to what is swept as one disappearing.
resolved_defects.round_4_the_module_set_was_the_hand_list: Round 4, and the same shape a third time: the fix reached less far than the claim. src/research_contracts/canonical/ holds EIGHT modules; the citation patterns alternated over SIX. Round 3 widened the TAIL and never touched the MODULE SET, so `engine` and `verification` were unscanned and FOUR live citations sat unread in the released packages/typescript/src/verification.ts -- verification.required_pin_fields, ._const_condition, ._conditional_pin_requirements, .conditional_pin_fields -- every one resolving in verification.py, every one in the identical `Mirrors Python's ...` idiom as the eight round 3 was written to rescue. The claim '3 of 20 -> 11 of 11' was really 11 of 15. Worse, the test's own docstring read 'derived from the documents rather than a hand-listed table' while exactly such a table sat beside it and _module_symbols derived from the AST one function away. BOTH the module set and the ambiguous-name set are now computed from the filesystem: modules from canonical/*.py, and a module counts as ambiguously named iff a TypeScript source of the same stem exists. A ninth module is scanned the day it is created. Widening also had to land WITH the filename fix: EXTENSIONS.md cites `packages/typescript/test/verification.test.ts`, and the extension lookahead guarded only the FIRST tail segment, so adding `verification` immediately fabricated the symbol `test.ts` -- and guarding every segment was still not enough, because the greedy tail simply BACKTRACKED to `tes`, which is followed by `t` rather than by `.ts`. It takes two lookaheads: one forbidding an end mid-identifier, one forbidding an end immediately before a file extension.
resolved_defects.round_4_the_resolver_half_had_no_control: Every control accumulated over rounds 2 and 3 targeted the PATTERN (what is scanned) or the FLOORS (how much). Nothing targeted the RESOLVER -- the half that actually kills a rename -- and five separate resolver mutations were green against the whole 1269-test suite: `assert not problems` turned into a tautology, a symbol table whose __contains__ always answers True, collecting every ast.Name so any identifier resolves, case-insensitive membership, and resolving only the FIRST segment of a dotted tail. That last one ships hash_view._ViewBuilder._no_such green -- the exact _ViewBuilder defect this repository already corrected once, and precisely what the nested-tail control was added to prevent, because that control pins the pattern's CAPTURE and not the resolver's USE of it. The resolver is now an extracted function exercised against SYNTHETIC text: a fabricated symbol must be reported, a correct one must not, a nested tail must resolve WHOLE, membership must be case-sensitive, and the symbol table must hold DEFINITIONS rather than every identifier (locals and parameters must not resolve).
resolved_defects.round_4_the_residue_was_understated_by_a: The round-3 docstring called the TypeScript residue 'a Python symbol with no underscore (jcs.canonicalize)'. Because the ambiguous arm required an underscore in the tail, it could not see the CamelCase class namespace at all: all ELEVEN exception classes in errors.py plus registry.CanonicalValidator -- and errors.ts's own header says 'The class NAMES are load-bearing ... a rename here silently decouples this port from the Python reference', which is exactly the names the gate could not check. The rule is now 'starts with a capital OR contains an underscore', which recovers all of them. MEASURED residue afterwards: ONE symbol, jcs.canonicalize, across six ambiguously-named modules. That number was first written as 4 from a guess and the package corrected it to 1; it is now computed and pinned rather than described.
resolved_defects.round_4_smaller_corrections: (a) A .ts source in a SUBDIRECTORY of src/ was invisible: both the sweep and the byte-equality backstop used a non-recursive glob('*.ts'), and the count equality could not catch it because the count did not move. Both are rglob now, matching package.json's lint script and both tsconfigs. (b) The two prose floors carried five slack each, and five was enough to absorb a real narrowing -- pairing the ambiguous pattern with EXTENSIONS.md dropped it 30 to 28 and stayed green, while the .ts floors, already exact, caught the same narrowing. All floors are EXACT counts now. (c) 'thirteen'/'the other twelve' was wrong: there are ELEVEN .ts sources, a number that sat eight lines from EXPECTED_TS_SOURCES = 11 contradicting it. (d) The astral mirror's cross-language comparison was one-directional. (e) The FALSE-POSITIVE direction is now stated and pinned at zero rather than hoped away: `errors` is a live local variable in several src files and snake_case dotted access is this repository's normal style, so `errors.failure_summary` would be reported as a citation resolving to nothing. No regex separates that from a real citation; the trade is deliberate, because a fabricated finding is loud and a missed citation is silent.

resolved_defects.title: An unregistered x-datacompany-* annotation name is preserved and ignored
resolved_defects.as_recorded: EXTENSIONS.md section 7.1: 'x-datacompany-hash-exclude (one letter short) is a valid JSON Schema member, is preserved on round-trip, and is read by nothing. The path stays in the hash view and no error is raised anywhere.'
resolved_defects.taken: Both engines now CONSULT the meta-schema at derivation, exactly as decision F made the cross-field path consult it: hash_profile._require_released_annotations (Python) and requireReleasedAnnotations (TypeScript) run on every node the derivation walk reaches, before anything is read off it, and raise a catchable HashProfileError with byte-identical message text. No new normative semantics were introduced and none were available to introduce: schemas/meta/datacompany-extension-vocabulary.v1.schema.json already rejected every shape below, under test_the_meta_schema_rejects_each_malformed_annotation, which is falsifiable one mutation at a time. What was missing was the engines consulting it. For this entry specifically: any x-datacompany-* member whose name is outside #/$defs/vocabulary is refused. The seven released names are re-stated as hash_profile._VOCABULARY. x-datacompany-composition-point was IN that set and, WHEN THIS CHANGE WAS MADE, was read by no code in either language -- recognising a name is not implementing it, so this entry left its value unconstrained, and a committed control asserted exactly that, so section 6.4 could not be closed by accident. That is a record of what this change did and is not a description of the vocabulary today: section 6.4 was closed as EXT-6.4, the annotation now has readers, and the control was renamed and repurposed with it. The control is deliberately NOT named here. resolved_defects.title: The exclusion cascade filtered `arrays` by exact match while filtering everything else by prefix
resolved_defects.as_recorded: EXTENSIONS.md section 5.2, 'STILL OPEN after WS1 -- inconsistency in the exclusion cascade, recorded not resolved': included_pointers and opaque_pointers were filtered by `pointer == excluded or pointer.startswith(excluded + "/")` while `arrays` was filtered by exact match only, so an array nested under an excluded subtree survived in the manifest. Excluding /sig dropped /sig/parts from included_pointers and /sig/blob from opaque_pointers but left {"pointer": "/sig/parts", "kind": "ordered"} in `arrays`. The section offered two remedies: reproduce the quirk, or change both engines together with a profile_version bump. Section 9 item 6 ordered every port to reproduce it.
resolved_defects.taken: The SECOND remedy. Both engines now filter `arrays` by the same at-or-under predicate as the other two members, and section 9 item 6 is deleted. DERIVATION_PROFILE_VERSION moved 1 -> 2 in the same change as every committed manifest, every embedded manifest byte in the D9 fixtures, and the differential-fuzz generator (which carried a HARDCODED 1 that would have survived the bump in silence -- it does not call derive_hash_profile, so nothing would have gone red while it fed both engines a manifest at a version neither implements).
resolved_defects.rejected: Fixing without bumping on the grounds that the observable delta is zero. That hollows out the constant on its first real test. DERIVATION_PROFILE_VERSION exists precisely so a derivation-rule change cannot happen silently: it is pinned in code, so editing it immediately failed every committed manifest still carrying 1 and forced one reviewable change touching the code, both engines and all seven manifests together. A version that only moves when the BYTES move cannot answer the one question it exists to answer -- which cascade derived the manifest in front of me. Also rejected: reproducing the quirk (remedy one), which would have left every conformant port choosing between agreeing with this engine and being internally consistent.
resolved_defects.hash_impact: NONE on the committed corpus, and the framing matters more than the number. Measured across all 18 released schemas by walking each with _Walker directly: 24 x-datacompany-array declarations and 38 exclusions exist, and ZERO arrays sit at or under an exclusion -- so re-deriving before and after diffs EMPTY (normalising profile_version out), and the seven regenerated manifests differ from their committed selves by exactly one line each, the version. POSITIVE CONTROL, on point: planting section 5.2's own worked example onto bitemporal-assertion:1 -- an excluded /sig containing an array at /sig/parts -- derives arrays ['/basis_refs', '/sig/parts'] on main and ['/basis_refs'] on the branch, so the harness can see the rule change. CORRECT FRAMING: the empty diff proves the fix is INERT ON THIS CORPUS, which is the blast-radius question, and NOT that it is correct. Deleting the arrays exclusion filter entirely produces the identical zero for the identical reason. Correctness rests on the synthetic probes and their mutations, not on the delta. Every previously computed content_hash is unaffected: no hash view changes, only the manifest's declared rule-set version.
resolved_defects.evidence: tests/test_canonical_hash.py::test_an_array_nested_under_an_exclusion_is_dropped_from_the_manifest and ::test_an_array_exactly_at_an_exclusion_is_still_dropped, mirrored in packages/typescript/test/manifests.test.ts ('drops an array nested UNDER an exclusion' / 'still drops an array EXACTLY at an exclusion'). Each probe carries a /survivor array OUTSIDE the exclusion, without which a filter that dropped every array would pass.
